sentences.text: Bransonella was an extinct genus of marine xenacanth that lived during the Paleozoic era.
Its teeth were small, measuring no more than 2 millimeters, suggesting the animal did not exceed one meter in length.
The creature possessed tiny teeth no larger than 2 millimeters, indicating a total body size under one meter.
The first species described, B. tridentata, was initially misidentified as a conodont in 1933.
The genus Bransonella was originally described by Harlton in 1933.
Researchers suggest Bransonella lived a lifestyle similar to modern catsharks, feeding on trilobites, crustaceans, gastropods, and occasionally small fish.
Bransonella belongs to the parent group Bransonelliformes.
Bransonella lived from the Tournaisian to the Roadian stages, between 358.86 and 266.9 million years ago.
B. nebraskensis has been found in the late Pennsylvanian of Nebraska and the middle Mississippian to early Permian of Kansas, the Urals, Poland, Belgium, Russia, and England.
B. lingulata is known from the Serpukhovian stage of Russia.
B. tribula was described from the middle Permian Kaibab formation of Arizona.
Additional fossils of Bransonella have been reported from the Mississippian of China and Australia, and the Pennsylvanian of Hungary and Brazil.
Bransonella was used to establish a new order alongside Barbclabornia based on specific ornamentation features.
